metric_rationale: By design, all trials in this experiment oppose Take The Best (TTB) and Tallying. The highest-validity discriminating cue always points to one option, while a numerical majority of lower-validity cues points to the other. This metric simply calculates the proportion of subject choices that match the TTB prediction. Data generated by TTB will yield a high value (close to 1.0, minus lapse noise), whereas data generated by Tallying will yield a low value (close to 0.0), strongly discriminating the two models.

Calculates the proportion of choices consistent with Tallying on trials where Tallying and Take The Best make strictly opposing predictions. Specifically, it isolates trials where the two options have an unequal number of positive cues. In this design, on all such trials, the option with more positive cues (favored by Tallying) is explicitly opposed by the highest-validity discriminating cue (favored by TTB). Therefore, Tallying will score near 1.0 on this metric, while Take The Best will score near 0.0, yielding a massive and highly reliable gap between the two theories.
